subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which wartime conference took place in February 1945, attended by Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin?
questions.explain: The Yalta Conference of February 1945 saw the Big Three agree on the post-war organisation of Europe.

questions.q: Who represented the United States for most of the Potsdam Conference in July-August 1945?
questions.explain: Truman had become President after Roosevelt's death in April 1945 and led the US delegation at Potsdam.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Truman Doctrine, announced in 1947?
options: To provide economic aid to rebuild Germany
To contain the spread of communism by supporting free peoples resisting it
To create a military alliance in Western Europe
To divide Berlin into four occupation zones
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine committed the USA to a policy of containment, offering support to countries threatened by communism.

questions.q: What was the Marshall Plan of 1947?
options: A programme of American economic aid to help rebuild Europe
A Soviet plan to coordinate communist parties
A treaty creating a Western military alliance
A plan to airlift supplies into Berlin
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan offered around $13 billion of US aid to rebuild European economies and resist communism.

questions.q: Which organisation did the USSR set up in 1949 to coordinate the economies of communist states in response to the Marshall Plan?
questions.explain: Comecon (1949) was the Soviet economic body intended to link the economies of the Eastern Bloc as a rival to Marshall Aid.

questions.q: How did the Western Allies respond to Stalin's blockade of West Berlin in 1948-49?
options: They withdrew their troops from the city
They organised an airlift to supply West Berlin
They launched a military attack on the blockade
They handed West Berlin over to the USSR
questions.explain: The Berlin Airlift flew in supplies for almost a year until Stalin lifted the blockade in May 1949.

questions.q: In which year was NATO formed as a Western defensive alliance?
questions.explain: NATO was created in April 1949 to provide collective defence for its Western members against the Soviet threat.

questions.q: In which year was the Warsaw Pact established as a military alliance of communist states?
questions.explain: The Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955, largely in response to West Germany being allowed to join NATO.

questions.q: On what date was the Berlin Wall first constructed?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was begun on 13 August 1961, sealing off West Berlin from the surrounding East.

questions.q: Why did the East German and Soviet authorities build the Berlin Wall in 1961?
options: To defend the city from a Western invasion
To stop the flow of refugees escaping to the West through West Berlin
To reunite the two halves of Germany
To provide a base for launching missiles
questions.explain: The Wall was built to halt the embarrassing loss of skilled workers fleeing East Germany via West Berlin.

questions.q: Who was the reforming Hungarian leader during the 1956 uprising?
questions.explain: Imre Nagy led the Hungarian reform government in 1956 and was later executed after the Soviet invasion.

questions.q: Which action by Nagy's government most alarmed the USSR and helped trigger the Soviet invasion of Hungary in 1956?
options: Announcing that Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact
Requesting Marshall Aid from the USA
questions.explain: Nagy's declaration that Hungary would withdraw from the Warsaw Pact and become neutral prompted Soviet military intervention.

questions.q: In which month and year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explain: The Cuban Missile Crisis unfolded over thirteen days in October 1962.

questions.q: How did President Kennedy immediately respond to the discovery of Soviet missiles on Cuba?
options: He ordered a naval blockade (quarantine) of Cuba
He launched an immediate nuclear strike
He invaded Cuba with ground troops
He removed all US missiles from Turkey publicly
questions.explain: Kennedy imposed a naval 'quarantine' to prevent further Soviet weapons reaching Cuba while negotiations took place.

questions.q: A student argues that the Cuban Missile Crisis, despite its danger, improved superpower communication. Which development best supports this claim?
options: The building of the Berlin Wall
The setting up of a telephone 'hotline' between Washington and Moscow
The creation of the Warsaw Pact
questions.explain: After the crisis a direct hotline was established in 1963 so leaders could communicate quickly and avoid future misunderstandings.

questions.q: As part of the settlement ending the Cuban Missile Crisis, what did Khrushchev secure in return for removing the missiles?
options: A US pledge not to invade Cuba
questions.explain: Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles in exchange for a public US promise not to invade Cuba, plus the secret removal of US missiles from Turkey.

questions.q: Who led the reform movement known as the Prague Spring in Czechoslovakia in 1968?
questions.explain: Alexander Dubcek introduced reforms aiming at 'socialism with a human face' during the 1968 Prague Spring.

questions.q: What was the main principle of the Brezhnev Doctrine, set out after the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia?
options: The USSR had the right to intervene in any communist state whose government was threatened
Communist states could freely leave the Warsaw Pact
The superpowers should share nuclear weapons
Western states should receive Soviet economic aid
questions.explain: The Brezhnev Doctrine asserted the USSR's right to use force to keep communist governments in power across the Eastern Bloc.

questions.q: What is meant by the term 'detente' in superpower relations?
options: A relaxation or easing of tension between the superpowers
An arms race between the USA and USSR
A total breakdown in diplomatic relations
A military alliance of communist states
questions.explain: Detente described the reduction of Cold War tensions and improved negotiation between East and West around the early 1970s.

questions.q: Which arms limitation agreement was signed by Nixon and Brezhnev in 1972?
questions.explain: The SALT 1 agreement of 1972 limited certain nuclear weapons and was a key achievement of detente.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE History (4HI1) specification; A World Divided: Superpower Relations 1943-72
